Chain Rule 21: Fractional Power of Shifted Sine

Course: Mathematics-I (Differential Calculus) Textbook Page: 32 | Problem: 21
প্রদত্ত সমীকরণ: y=sin⁡x−13বাy=(sin⁡x−1)13y = \sqrt[3]{\sin x - 1} \quad \text{বা} \quad y = (\sin x - 1)^{\frac{1}{3}}y=3sinx−1​বাy=(sinx−1)31​
নির্ণেয়: dydx\dfrac{dy}{dx}dxdy​
📘 English Note — Fractional Power Trigonometric Chain Rule Formulation
The problem is a composite function with a fractional cube root power and an inner trigonometric core: y=[g(x)]n  ⟹  dydx=n[g(x)]n−1⋅g′(x)y = [g(x)]^n \implies \frac{dy}{dx} = n[g(x)]^{n-1} \cdot g'(x)y=[g(x)]n⟹dxdy​=n[g(x)]n−1⋅g′(x) Here g(x)=sin⁡x−1g(x) = \sin x - 1g(x)=sinx−1 and n=13n = \frac{1}{3}n=31​: dydx=13(sin⁡x−1)13−1⋅ddx(sin⁡x−1)=cos⁡x3(sin⁡x−1)23=cos⁡x3(sin⁡x−1)23\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{3}(\sin x - 1)^{\frac{1}{3}-1} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}(\sin x - 1) = \frac{\cos x}{3(\sin x - 1)^{\frac{2}{3}}} = \frac{\cos x}{3\sqrt[3]{(\sin x - 1)^2}}dxdy​=31​(sinx−1)31​−1⋅dxd​(sinx−1)=3(sinx−1)32​cosx​=33(sinx−1)2​cosx​
১. গাণিতিক কাঠামো ও প্রয়োজনীয় সূত্রসমূহ
উপাদান (Component) ফাংশন রূপ প্রমিত সূত্র (Standard Derivative)
বহিঃস্থ ঘাত ফাংশন (Outer Power) u13u^{\frac{1}{3}}u31​ ddu(un)=nun−1  ⟹  ddu(u13)=13u−23\frac{d}{du}(u^n) = n u^{n-1} \implies \frac{d}{du}(u^{\frac{1}{3}}) = \frac{1}{3}u^{-\frac{2}{3}}dud​(un)=nun−1⟹dud​(u31​)=31​u−32​
অভ্যন্তরীণ পদ (Inner Trigonometric) u=sin⁡x−1u = \sin x - 1u=sinx−1 dudx=ddx(sin⁡x−1)=cos⁡x\frac{du}{dx} = \frac{d}{dx}(\sin x - 1) = \cos xdxdu​=dxd​(sinx−1)=cosx
সম্মিলিত চেইন রুল (sin⁡x−1)13(\sin x - 1)^{\frac{1}{3}}(sinx−1)31​ dydx=cos⁡x3(sin⁡x−1)23=cos⁡x3(sin⁡x−1)23\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{\cos x}{3(\sin x - 1)^{\frac{2}{3}}} = \frac{\cos x}{3\sqrt[3]{(\sin x - 1)^2}}dxdy​=3(sinx−1)32​cosx​=33(sinx−1)2​cosx​
২. ধাপে ধাপে পূর্ণাঙ্গ গাণিতিক সমাধান
ধাপ ১:
ঘনমূলকে ভগ্নাংশ সূচক আকারে প্রকাশ করে অন্তরীকরণ অপারেটর প্রয়োগ করি:
y=(sin⁡x−1)13  ⟹  dydx=ddx[(sin⁡x−1)13]y = (\sin x - 1)^{\frac{1}{3}} \implies \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{d}{dx}\left[(\sin x - 1)^{\frac{1}{3}}\right]y=(sinx−1)31​⟹dxdy​=dxd​[(sinx−1)31​]
ধাপ ২:
বহিঃস্থ ঘাত u13u^{\frac{1}{3}}u31​-এর ওপর Power Rule প্রয়োগ করে চেইন রুল বিস্তার করি:
dydx=13(sin⁡x−1)13−1⋅ddx(sin⁡x−1)=13(sin⁡x−1)−23⋅ddx(sin⁡x−1)\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{3}(\sin x - 1)^{\frac{1}{3} - 1} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}(\sin x - 1) = \frac{1}{3}(\sin x - 1)^{-\frac{2}{3}} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}(\sin x - 1)dxdy​=31​(sinx−1)31​−1⋅dxd​(sinx−1)=31​(sinx−1)−32​⋅dxd​(sinx−1)
ধাপ ৩:
অভ্যন্তরীণ পদ (sin⁡x−1)(\sin x - 1)(sinx−1)-এর ব্যবকলন ddx(sin⁡x−1)=cos⁡x\frac{d}{dx}(\sin x - 1) = \cos xdxd​(sinx−1)=cosx বসিয়ে পাই:
dydx=13(sin⁡x−1)−23⋅cos⁡x=13cos⁡x(sin⁡x−1)−23\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{3}(\sin x - 1)^{-\frac{2}{3}} \cdot \cos x = \frac{1}{3}\cos x (\sin x - 1)^{-\frac{2}{3}}dxdy​=31​(sinx−1)−32​⋅cosx=31​cosx(sinx−1)−32​
ধাপ ৪:
ঋণাত্মক সূচককে হরে এনে ধনাত্মক ঘাতে প্রমিত রূপান্তর করি:
dydx=cos⁡x3(sin⁡x−1)23=cos⁡x3(sin⁡x−1)23\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{\cos x}{3(\sin x - 1)^{\frac{2}{3}}} = \frac{\cos x}{3\sqrt[3]{(\sin x - 1)^2}}dxdy​=3(sinx−1)32​cosx​=33(sinx−1)2​cosx​
চূড়ান্ত প্রমিত উত্তর (Final Standard Answer)
dydx=13cos⁡x(sin⁡x−1)−23=cos⁡x3(sin⁡x−1)23\mathbf{\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{3}\cos x (\sin x - 1)^{-\frac{2}{3}} = \frac{\cos x}{3(\sin x - 1)^{\frac{2}{3}}}}dxdy​=31​cosx(sinx−1)−32​=3(sinx−1)32​cosx​

Chain Rule 21: Engineering & Rigorous Analysis

Course: Mathematics-I (Differential Calculus) Theoretical Foundations & Examination Blueprint
⚠️ English Note — Critical AMIE Exam Traps & Pitfalls
  • Trap 1 (Fractional Subtraction Error): Remember 13−1=−23\frac{1}{3} - 1 = -\frac{2}{3}31​−1=−32​. Do not mistakenly write 23\frac{2}{3}32​ or −13-\frac{1}{3}−31​.
  • Trap 2 (Omitting Inner Derivative cos⁡x\cos xcosx): Forgetting to multiply by ddx(sin⁡x−1)=cos⁡x\frac{d}{dx}(\sin x - 1) = \cos xdxd​(sinx−1)=cosx.
  • Trap 3 (Sign Integrity): ddx(sin⁡x−1)=+cos⁡x\frac{d}{dx}(\sin x - 1) = +\cos xdxd​(sinx−1)=+cosx (do not write −cos⁡x-\cos x−cosx).
🟣 English Note — Domain, Singularities & Cusp Points (AMIE Rigor)
  • Domain of Function: Real cube roots are defined for all real arguments, positive and negative: Dom(y)=(−∞,∞)=R\text{Dom}(y) = (-\infty, \infty) = \mathbb{R}Dom(y)=(−∞,∞)=R
  • Domain of Derivative: The derivative denominator requires sin⁡x−1≠0  ⟹  sin⁡x≠1\sin x - 1 \neq 0 \implies \sin x \neq 1sinx−1=0⟹sinx=1: Dom(dydx)=R∖{2kπ+π2  |  k∈Z}\text{Dom}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right) = \mathbb{R} \setminus \left\{ 2k\pi + \frac{\pi}{2} \;\middle|\; k \in \mathbb{Z} \right\}Dom(dxdy​)=R∖{2kπ+2π​​k∈Z}
  • Cusp Points / Vertical Tangent: As x→π2x \to \frac{\pi}{2}x→2π​, the slope lim⁡x→π/2dydx\lim_{x \to \pi/2} \frac{dy}{dx}limx→π/2​dxdy​ exhibits vertical tangent singularity.
💡 English Note — Formal Substitution Model
Let u=sin⁡x−1  ⟹  dudx=cos⁡xu = \sin x - 1 \implies \frac{du}{dx} = \cos xu=sinx−1⟹dxdu​=cosx.
Then y=u1/3  ⟹  dydu=13u−2/3=13u2/3y = u^{1/3} \implies \frac{dy}{du} = \frac{1}{3}u^{-2/3} = \frac{1}{3u^{2/3}}y=u1/3⟹dudy​=31​u−2/3=3u2/31​.
By Leibniz Chain Rule: dydx=dydu⋅dudx=13u2/3⋅cos⁡x=cos⁡x3(sin⁡x−1)2/3\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy}{du} \cdot \frac{du}{dx} = \frac{1}{3u^{2/3}} \cdot \cos x = \frac{\cos x}{3(\sin x - 1)^{2/3}}dxdy​=dudy​⋅dxdu​=3u2/31​⋅cosx=3(sinx−1)2/3cosx​
